correctness.rationale: On the mean-zero space the gap lower bound z is a positive-semidefinite constraint. Compressing to the group contrast and taking normalized traces on the two within-group zero-sum spaces gives the three necessary bounds on totals; uniform weights realize all three compressed Rayleigh values. At fixed z the minimum normalized cost therefore reduces to a piecewise-linear function of cross weight divided by z, with breakpoints 1/(p+q), 1/p, 1/q. The slopes are pq−t(2pq−p−q)/2 and pq−tq(p−1)/2, so the claimed values and flat intervals follow; for equal groups the last two breakpoints coalesce. At all points where both internal trace bounds are tight, positivity forces both within-group zero-sum spaces into the gap eigenspace. Applied across the partition this makes every column and row constant, and within each group it makes the internal Laplacian scalar on its zero-sum space. This proves the stated unrestricted uniqueness and the full lower and balanced critical segments. Above the upper price only the larger group's bound is tight: equal rows with slightly unequal positive column weights preserve the large group's eigenvalue B/p while the other positive eigenvalues remain strictly larger by continuity. For the explicit example 5u1u2=11/80>1/9. The upper endpoint claim is only an exhibited segment, not an exhaustion. The frozen NumPy checks were inspected as supporting evidence, not run or treated as the proof.

evidence: Sun et al. p. 683 is exactly the rate-budget maximum-gap formulation, and §4.1 gives the maximum variance unfolding dual.

The earlier two-block specialization charges (cross, larger internal, smaller internal) = (1,t,1) instead of (1,t,t); for p>q≥2 and t≠1 its t-price subgraph is one clique plus isolates, not two cliques on all vertices. Its unit-price subgraph is connected with triangles, not a complete bipartite graph.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Continuous-time consensus, fastest diffusion, and fastest mixing refer to the same unnormalized symmetric spectral-gap optimization here. Neither relabeling nor normalization changes the earlier edge-price pattern into the target pattern, even if the two relative prices are interchanged.

evidence: The closest unequal two-block record has a different lower price and asserts uniqueness only in the orbit-constant class. Resultary da6bd4b37466 covers the equal-size optimum value, decision threshold and symmetric optimal set, but explicitly does not assert arbitrary-design uniqueness. Other indexed models price a matching in a complete graph or alternating classes on an even cycle.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The balanced formula and symmetric phase diagram are demonstrably covered, but none of the matching statements gives the unequal optimizer classification or even excludes nonsymmetric balanced ties. Their dates do not decide equivalence or priority.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected priced complete-graph theorem shares the method and the upper price but changes one block's relative price and does not give the target lower transition or unrestricted rigidity. Credit the framework and shared upper-price calculation; the distinct content is the two-internal-price law and rigidity/nonrigidity classification under independent weights.
residual_risks: A different or unindexed explicit budgeted-SDP specialization may give equivalent results; the inspected overlap does not.
